about: The site's addresses, held to one table by web/test/permalinks.test.mjs (web/scripts/permalinks.mjs) and tests/Lex.V3.Tests/V3WebRootTests.cs (V3WebRoot). `page`: the page a law's address under an interface language is served; `redirect`: where a path with no interface language is sent, for a reader whose browser names no language (French, R61); `moved`: where a permalink of the shape before R64 (an EU wording's /eu-eurlex/{celex}/{lng}/{date}--{sha256}) has moved for good, whatever the reader's language, and where a consolidated version's readable address (/eu-eurlex/0{act}-{yyyymmdd}/{lng}[/{provision}]) has moved, to its act's (/eu-eurlex/3{act}/{lng}[/{provision}]; review of #972); none of them: the path is left to the files and the API's routing, as a Luxembourg state's permalink before R64 (/lu-legilux/{work}/{date}--{sha256}, which names no language) is. `languages`: the interface language each Accept-Language starts a reader in. `render`: for a served page, what the server renders it from (R67): its language, the page, and the operation and parameters the page itself would ask: at a permalink, the permalink itself with no article (R64: the version it pins, or pinned_digest_mismatch with the current link), its date and its language; at an act's readable address (/lu-legilux/{work}/{lng}[/{article}], /eu-eurlex/{celex}/{lng}[/{provision}], R67: the current version), the work, `today` (the date in Luxembourg the table is held at, R13) and the language. A readable address's article is never a calendar date, with or without a digest: /eu-eurlex/{celex}/{lng}/{date} is an EU stable coordinate and /eu-eurlex/{celex}/{lng}/{date}--{sha256} the EU shape before R64; an interface language's home page (`/fr/`, `/en/`, and each one's `index.html`) is the file the directory holds, rendered from `coverage` with no parameters (the home page's facts, R11 and R13). `canonical`, on the rows of the work and state the evidence_bundle sample answers (schemas/v3-platform/envelope-samples.json, "the work on its state's date"): the canonical link that page names rendered from that answer, by the web's server renderer of the path's interface language, which both servers run (review of #967: an address the platform mints, never the request's own; web/test/live-ssr.test.mjs), under that interface language (the plan's item 3.6: a page that answers itself, never an address that redirects); at a readable address, the readable address of the article when the version shown holds it, else the act's; at a permalink whose version is the one its act's readable address shows today (the sample's state, applicable from 2024-02-01 with no later state, answered on 2026-09-18), that readable address (R67: "identical version pages point their canonical link there"). An article segment that is `.` or `..` once decoded (`%2E`, `.%2e`) is no article.

searchEngines.about: What the site says to search engines (the specification of record's R67; the plan's item 3.6), held to one table by web/test/search-engines.test.mjs (web/scripts/search-engines.mjs, serve-live.mjs) and tests/Lex.V3.Tests/V3WebRootSearchEnginesTests.cs (V3WebRoot.SearchEngines.cs). `variable` is the release's switch, read by both servers when they start; `states` the state each value of it gives (only `indexed` opens; anything else, its absence included, is kept out: the owner has not answered O27). `meta` the two robots elements a live page carries: `never` on a page no search engine is ever asked to index, `keptOut` on one the switch opens, which a server removes with the site indexed when the page may be (`pages`). `robots` robots.txt in each state; `record` an indexing record (R92's outcome: the works its measurement found to name no private individual, with the text languages of their readable addresses), `admitted` and `refused` records each reader takes or refuses whole, and `sitemap` the sitemap with the site indexed and `record` held (no record: the home pages and Trust and Coverage only). `pages`: for a page that carries the kept-out marker at `path`, whether a server opens it (removes the marker and the X-Robots-Tag header) in each state, with `record` held, or with none. The rows /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml under `paths` say what each server answers there in each state (`claimed` false: an address the site does not hold, its 404).
